content: An analysis of the impact of municipal fibre regulations on internet accessibility in South Africa between 2020 and 2023 reveals a highly positive trajectory in broadband penetration. During this period, Internet Accessibility Penetration demonstrated an overall increasing trend, beginning at a minimum value of 65.0 percent in 2020 and steadily climbing to reach a maximum value of 82.0 percent by 2023. This significant growth underscores the critical role that infrastructure expansion and progressive regulatory adjustments have played in connecting broader segments of the population. While detailed archival records of specific municipal fibre regulations from the 2020 to 2023 timeframe are largely superseded by current directives, the empirical data clearly illustrates that the operational environment during those years facilitated substantial gains in connectivity. The momentum generated during this period has set the foundation for subsequent regulatory reforms aimed at further accelerating network deployment and addressing residual inefficiencies. As of June 2026, the regulatory discourse has shifted toward proactive measures designed to eliminate systemic barriers to infrastructure rollout. The Independent Communications Authority of South Africa (ICASA) has been instrumental in this regard, recently introducing draft regulations aimed specifically at the rapid deployment of electronic communication networks [123] . These draft regulations, which were open for public consultation until late May 2026, represent a pivotal step toward standardizing deployment procedures across different municipalities, thereby reducing the administrative friction that has historically delayed fibre-optic installations [123] . By establishing a more uniform and expedited approval process, ICASA intends to facilitate faster time-to-market for network operators, directly benefiting entities like Vcom that rely on agile infrastructure expansion to maintain competitive advantage. For Vcom, the harmonization of municipal regulations under this new policy framework presents a strategic opportunity to accelerate its fibre footprint in previously constrained urban and peri-urban areas, thereby capturing new subscriber bases and enhancing service delivery.
